topics.title: 11.1.1 Distinguishing Linearizable, Sequential, and Eventual Views
topics.summary: A linearizable operation behaves as if it took effect at one point between its invocation and completion, while respecting real-time precedence between completed operations. Sequential consistency preserves a single order consistent with each participant’s program order but does not add the same real-time requirement. Eventual consistency describes convergence under suitable conditions; by itself it leaves many details of intermediate reads and conflicts unspecified.

topics.title: 11.1.2 Describing Session Guarantees and Read Dependencies
topics.summary: Read-your-writes means a session can observe its own completed writes under the service’s stated conditions. Monotonic reads prevent a session from moving backward through versions already observed. These are useful requirements when a fully global ordering is unnecessary, but they still need implementation mechanisms.

topics.title: 11.2.1 Separating Receipt, Persistence, and Application
topics.summary: A follower can receive bytes, append them to a log, flush them according to a storage contract, and apply them to its state machine at different moments. “The follower has the write” is ambiguous unless it identifies the stage. A read from that follower can lag even after it has received the log entry.

blocks.text: The leader’s acknowledgement policy defines which failures can lose an acknowledged write. Acknowledging after only local memory differs from acknowledging after durable storage on a quorum. Neither policy is meaningfully evaluated without naming the failure domains: several processes on the same disk are not independent durable copies against loss of that disk.

blocks.text: Replication also copies more than business rows. Idempotency records, sequence positions, schema metadata, and authorization-relevant state may participate in the correctness boundary. If a new leader has the job effect but not its receipt, a retry can produce a duplicate. If it has a receipt whose referenced effect was not retained, it can claim work that disappeared.

topics.title: 11.2.2 Recovering Lagging Replicas Without Inventing Authority
topics.summary: A lagging replica may replay a retained log or install a snapshot and then catch up from a corresponding position. The snapshot must represent a consistent state, and the replay position must match it. Combining a snapshot from one point with an unrelated log cursor can omit or repeat changes.

topics.title: 11.3.1 Applying CAP to the Failure Case It Describes
topics.summary: The CAP result concerns the inability to guarantee both the specified consistency and availability properties in a system that can experience network partitions. Its availability notion is not simply an uptime percentage, and its consistency notion is not a generic synonym for valid data. Treating it as a permanent instruction to “pick any two” obscures the actual partition case. (R17)

reading.title: 11.3.1 Applying CAP to the Failure Case It Describes
paragraphs: The CAP result concerns the inability to guarantee both the specified consistency and availability properties in a system that can experience network partitions. Its availability notion is not simply an uptime percentage, and its consistency notion is not a generic synonym for valid data. Treating it as a permanent instruction to “pick any two” obscures the actual partition case. (R17)

During a partition, two groups may be unable to communicate. A design that requires a single ordered authority may reject some operations on the side that cannot establish that authority. A design that accepts updates independently must define how conflicts are represented and reconciled, if reconciliation is possible for the operation.

Some operations combine naturally; others do not. Independent additions to a suitable counter can be easier to merge than two claims on the last seat in a venue. The business invariant determines whether concurrent acceptance is acceptable. A generic merge function cannot undo every externally observed promise.

For HarborDispatch, allowing isolated workers with independent receipt stores to execute the same key would expand availability but weaken the promised effect boundary. Calling the system “eventually consistent” would not explain how a duplicate external action should be repaired.

blocks.text: Degradation must remain observable. Operators need to distinguish “no new jobs were submitted” from “all new jobs were rejected,” and clients need to distinguish “not found” from “cannot obtain a sufficiently current read.” Collapsing these outcomes into one empty response produces misleading dashboards and unsafe retries.

blocks.text: Recovery also needs a policy for queued work. When a dependency returns, replay can overwhelm it. Restored connectivity does not instantly restore normal service if hours of work remain pending.

paragraphs: Imagine a three-replica store with a leader L and followers F1 and F2. A new record exists only in L’s memory when L responds success. L then loses both process memory and its local disk. Neither follower has the record. The client observed success under a policy that did not preserve the write against this failure.

Now consider a different policy requiring the relevant durable replication and commitment conditions before success. That policy may survive the same leader loss if the surviving replicas retain the committed state and the protocol safely elects a new leader. The difference is not the number of boxes in the diagram; it is the acknowledgement rule and recovery protocol.

Do not shorten the second policy to “two copies means safe.” The copies may share a failure domain, the follower may only have received bytes without persisting them, or the new leader selection may ignore the committed log requirement. Quorum arithmetic must be connected to actual persistence and protocol rules.

A read adds another stage. F1 might have persisted a log entry but not yet applied it to its query state. Routing a read to F1 without an applied-revision check can still return an older value. Replication receipt, commit, application, and read eligibility remain distinct.

For an idempotent operation, include the receipt in the replicated state. If only the visible result survives, a retry may be indistinguishable from a new operation. If only the receipt survives but its referenced effect is missing, the service can replay a false success. The atomic relationship among these records is part of what replication must preserve.

The companion’s replica model deliberately omits all of this machinery. Its purpose is to make lag visible, not to imply a high-availability store. The integrated service uses local SQLite files and states its recovery scope accordingly.
